newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says PLO state would end peace moves.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says PLO state would end peace moves.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that the PLO would bring peace moves to a halt if it unilaterally declared a Palestinian state now.

"And if someone wants to declare, today, the establishment of a Palestinian state, let him do it. It will be a serious mistake, a severe mistake, that will bring a halt to the entire process," Netanyahu told members of his Likud party in Tel Aviv.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Saturday that he could declare a Palestinian state in reaction to the approval by Netanyahu's government last Wednesday to build a new settlement for Jews in Arab East Jerusaelem.
Netanyahu said, as he has in the past, that Israel had a plan in place to deal with the unilateral declaration of a Palestinian state he has vowed he will never allow. But he did not elaborate.
"We will know how to react and what to do and how to protect the assets," he said.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised by the international community it annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital.

The Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the occupied territories with East Jerusalem as capital. According to interim peace deals, the two sides are to reach a final peace accord in 1999.
Earlier on Sunday, Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said a declaration of a state would be "a very serious violation of agreements" the Palestine Liberation Organisation had signed with Israel.
Arafat told an emergency session of the Arab League in Cairo on Saturday:

"We are supposed to declare the setting up of a Palestinian state in five years but what would happen if I declare it right here? What would he (Netanyahu) do then? It's tit-for-tat and we have our weapons too."

Israel's approval on Wednesday of a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim, a tree-lined hill in Arab East Jerusalem called Har Homa by Israel, sparked international criticism and Palestinian warnings it could unleash bloodshed.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Sunday that, for now, Arafat was preventing an outburst of violence.
"The Palestinian Authority has made every effort not to come into direct confrontation (with Israel)," said Mordechai in remarks broadcast on Israel's army radio.
"Nobody knows what will happen when the tractors begin working at Har Homa or when Arafat concludes after his visit in Washington that doesn't serve all his interests," he said.
Arafat is to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Monday.

Under a deal in which Israel handed 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January, Israel committed to a timetable for three more withdrawals of undetermined size from rural areas of the West Bank.
The first of the pullbacks is to be by March 7.
Netanyahu's office said on Sunday that the government would meet on March 6, to vote on the pullback.
"Immediately after the cabinet decides it will be implemented," a Netanyahu spokesman said.
